raw_case_text: A 54-year-old female was referred to our department with blurred vision and metamorphopsia in her left eye following the diagnosis of DF 2 weeks earlier. She presented all classic systemic symptoms of DF with a papular rash over her arms and hands followed by fever, headache, retro-orbital pain and myalgia. A systemic workup revealed a thrombocytopenia, and a real-time PCR for the dengue virus type 2 was positive, confirming the diagnosis of DF. Noteworthy, she reported 2 previous episodes of DF in 2009 and 2011. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/150 in the left eye. An anterior segment examination showed no abnormalities. Ophthalmoscopy revealed subretinal fluid and focal hemorrhage in the macula of the left eye (fig. 1a). A fluorescein angiography (FA) showed a hyperfluorescent lesion with well-defined borders and active leakage consistent with classic CNV (fig. 1b). A spectral domain OCT [SD-OCT; Spectralis OCTTM (Heidelberg Engineering, Heidelberg, Germany)] revealed subretinal fluid and focal hyperreflective material in the subretinal space as well as an area with small retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) detachments (fig. 1c). The patient was referred to receive 3 monthly intravitreal injections of ranibizumab (Lucentis; Novartis, Basel, Switzerland, and Genentech, Inc., South San Francisco, Calif., USA). After this loading dose, her BCVA improved to 20/25 in the left eye, and there also was a marked anatomical improvement (fig. 1d). After 6 months, her BCVA was still 20/25 in the left eye and the SD-OCT remained without any signs of active CNV. Two years later, the patient again presented to our service complaining about a reduced VA in her left eye. The BCVA was 20/30 and the FA showed a leaking lesion temporal to and another site of leakage inferior to the fovea. Indocyanine green angiography revealed focal hot spots in these areas (fig. 2a, b). SD-OCT showed marked subretinal fluid, an increased extension of RPE detachments and RPE discontinuity, discrete intraretinal cysts and hyperreflective subretinal material (fig. 2c). The patient underwent 2 monthly intravitreal injections of ranibizumab with functional and anatomical improvement. The BCVA improved to 20/25, but there was persistence of fibrovascular RPE detachment (fig. 2d). Six months later, her VA had returned to 20/20 and OCT showed an absence of disease activity. Regular follow-up visits were recommended.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old female presented with blurred vision and metamorphopsia in her left eye 2 weeks after an episode of acute dengue fever, followed by recurrent left visual reduction 2 years later.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two weeks before ophthalmic referral, the patient experienced classic dengue fever with a papular rash over her arms and hands followed by fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, and myalgia. She then developed left-eye blurred vision and metamorphopsia, responded to anti-VEGF therapy, and represented 2 years later with recurrent reduced visual acuity in the left eye.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of two prior episodes of dengue fever in 2009 and 2011, plus a third episode 2 weeks prior to initial ophthalmic presentation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left-eye blurred vision and metamorphopsia, preceded 2 weeks earlier by papular arm/hand rash, fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, and myalgia.

objective.physical_examination: Initial ophthalmic exam: BCVA 20/20 OD and 20/150 OS, normal anterior segment exam, and left macular subretinal fluid and focal hemorrhage on ophthalmoscopy (improving to BCVA 20/25 after initial treatment). Two years later: BCVA 20/30 OS, improving to 20/25 and subsequently 20/20 at 6 months after retreatment.
objective.routine_investigations: Systemic workup during acute illness showed thrombocytopenia. Initial fluorescein angiography (FA) OS showed a well-defined hyperfluorescent lesion with active leakage consistent with classic choroidal neovascularization (CNV); SD-OCT showed subretinal fluid, subretinal hyperreflective material, and small retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) detachments. At 2-year recurrence, FA showed temporal and inferior juxtafoveal leakage, indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) showed focal hot spots, and SD-OCT showed marked subretinal fluid, expanded RPE detachments/discontinuity, intraretinal cysts, and subretinal hyperreflective material.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Dengue maculopathy complicated by secondary choroidal neovascularization (CNV) and pachychoroid/polypoidal-like recurrence following tertiary DENV-2 infection, confirmed by positive DENV-2 real-time RT-PCR, FA/ICGA, and SD-OCT. Treated initially with 3 monthly intravitreal ranibizumab injections (improving BCVA from 20/150 to 20/25) and retreated at 2-year recurrence with 2 monthly intravitreal ranibizumab injections, achieving complete resolution of disease activity and 20/20 visual acuity at 6-month follow-up.
